888 is the conceptual motif, not an octal numeral. Octal has eight digit states, 0 through 7. The quantity eight is written 10₈; the completed 512-state A8 whole is written 1000₈.

DISPLAY MODE — switches the whole page

Rule: map 512 + clock 512 + compass 512, or map 1000₈ + clock 1000₈ + compass 1000₈. Never cross the two views.

1. One Ruler Everywhere

MAP — LONGITUDE FULL WRAP
CLOCK — FULL-DAY PHASE RING
COMPASS — FULL TURN
MAP — LATITUDE POLE TO POLE (HALF TURN)

Longitude, clock phase and compass bearing are the same complete 512-state turn expressed in the selected notation. Latitude is a half-turn from North Pole to South Pole, so it ends at 256 decimal / 400₈.

4. Map Reference — one complete map per mode

DECIMAL 512 MAP. This is the original accepted decimal map, unchanged: longitude 0…512 and latitude 0…256.

Switching to Octal mode replaces the entire map with the same underlying Earth/grid relabeled as longitude 000₈…1000₈ and latitude 000₈…400₈. No decimal A8 labels are carried into the octal map.

5. Quick Coordinate Converter — corrected notation

This converter outputs only the currently selected A8 display mode. Conventional latitude is hard-limited to −90…+90 and conventional longitude to −180…+180. Values such as 181° are rejected rather than silently wrapped.

INPUT DOMAIN Latitude: −90° … +90° Longitude: −180° … +180° A8_LAT = (90 − conventional_latitude) × 256 / 180 For conventional longitude λ: if λ ≥ 0: eastward λE = λ if λ < 0: eastward λE = 360 + λ A8_LON = λE × 512 / 360 ±180° are the same opposite meridian: +180° = −180° = A8 256 = 400₈ Longitude output wraps only at the A8 ruler: 0 / 512 decimal ↔ 000 / 1000₈ octal Latitude does not wrap: North 0 → Equator 128 → South 256 North 000₈ → Equator 200₈ → South 400₈

7. Clock Representation

Shared outer phase ruler

Full day phase: Decimal view = 0 → 512 Octal view = 000₈ → 1000₈ 32 A8 hours per day 512 / 32 = 16 decimal phase units per hour 16 decimal = 20₈ phase units per hour

Clock fields follow the same mode

Decimal mode: HH = 00…31 MM = 00…63 SS = 00…63 Octal mode: HH = 00…37₈ MM = 00…77₈ SS = 00…77₈

The outer day phase and the HH:MM:SS decomposition describe the same 32×64×64 = 2¹⁷ daily states.

8. What Never Changes

Same Earth · same west-to-east rotation · same compass directions · same great circles · same 512 physical states. Only the notation view changes.

9. City & Route Atlas

Distance-rung principle: the quartz-derived length quantity is fixed. A larger or smaller A8/n rung is only an exact binary display scale. Physical uncertainty remains physical; changing rung introduces no conversion approximation.

Real-world adoption layer: major cities can be placed into A8 hour sectors, given A8 decimal or octal coordinates, and connected by route distances using the same unified display mode as the map, clock and compass.

This atlas stays inside the same discipline: same Earth, same cities, same geometry, new ruler only. A8 values are shown first. Operating-time examples are published only when a source or explicit calculation is identified; otherwise the route remains a geometric distance reference.

Route reference

Route A8 navigation distance Elapsed travel reference Legacy geometry check

Navigation distance display: this atlas now uses the provisional rung 240qa because it gives human-scale route numbers. In Decimal mode the rung is labeled A8/40; in hard Octal the same exponent is A8/50₈ because 40₁₀ = 50₈. The rung changes the display scale, not the physical distance.

A8 elapsed time is shown first. 1 A8 hour = 45 legacy minutes, so legacy elapsed hours × 4/3 = A8 hours. A day remains the same physical full-day interval: 24 legacy hours = 32 A8 hours. Local clock changes and date-line changes do not alter elapsed travel time.

Derived from Japan Airlines' published March 29–October 24, 2026 Tokyo→Los Angeles schedule and the applicable JST/PDT offset. Schedule times can change; this is an example, not a definition of A8 time.

Sea — navigation benchmark @ 20 kn

Great-circle ≈ 4,800 nmi: (240 legacy h) = 10 days

Rhumb-line ≈ 5,100 nmi: (255 legacy h) = 10.625 days

MOL's navigation example gives approximately 4,800 nmi great-circle and 5,100 nmi rhumb-line distance between Los Angeles and Tokyo. MOL also notes that actual routing considers weather, sea conditions and tidal currents.

Important: the ≈10.5-day neighborhood can arise from route geometry at about 20 kn; it must not be created by adding or subtracting time-zone or date-line changes. Elapsed time and local displayed time are separate quantities.

Sources checked 16 Aug 2026: Japan Airlines — North America route schedule · MOL — Routes and Speed of Cargo Ship. External links open only when selected; the instrument itself makes no network requests.
